title: Sajith calls for meaningful empowerment in New Year message
byline: Opposition Leader Sajith Premadasa has called for meaningful empowerment of the people through sustainable, long-term solutions in his message marking the Sinhala and Tamil New Year.

title: Man arrested at BIA with illegal cigarette stock
byline: Katunayake, April 14 (Daily Mirror) - A Sri Lankan passenger was arrested by airport customs officers in the early hours of April 14 for attempting to illegally bring a large consignment of foreign-made cigarettes into the country through the “Green Channel” at the arrivals terminal of Bandaranaike International Airport (BIA).

title: PM extends New Year wishes to nation
byline: Prime Minister Harini Amarasuriya has extended her wishes to the nation in a message marking the Sinhala and Tamil New Year, highlighting unity, renewal and collective strength.

title: President’s New Year message highlights unity, prosperity and renewal
byline: Marking the auspicious transition of the sun and the arrival of the spring harvest season, the Sinhala and Tamil New Year has dawned once again, celebrated by Sri Lankans since ancient times.

title: Beginning of the New Year
byline: The Sinhala and Hindu (Tamil) New Year will begin on Tuesday, April 14, at 9:32 AM according to the first part of the day.

title: Trump deletes post depicting him as Jesus-like figure after backlash
byline: Faced with growing backlash, US President Donald Trump appears to have removed a controversial Truth Social post depicting himself as a Jesus-like figure.

title: Police urge caution as road fatalities rise during festive season
byline: Sri Lanka Police have issued a strong warning to motorists to avoid drunk and reckless driving during the ongoing festive season.

title: US State Department confirms Rubio to take part in Lebanon-Israel talks
byline: The US State Department has confirmed that Secretary of State Marco Rubio will take part in Tuesday’s meeting between the Lebanese and Israeli ambassadors to Washington.

title: Nonagathaya begins
byline: The Nonagathaya or inauspicious time for the New Year will be observed from 3:08 AM to 3:56 PM on Tuesday, April 14.

title: Protect children from fireworks: Health officials
byline: Authorities have urged parents to keep children away from firecrackers during the festive season, citing rising injury risks.

title: Ukrainian woman arrested over assault on Sri Lankan in Mount Lavinia
byline: A Ukrainian national was arrested late last night for allegedly behaving in a disorderly manner and assaulting a Sri Lankan woman in Mount Lavinia, Police said.

title: Landslide warnings issued for four districts
byline: The National Building Research Organisation (NBRO) has issued landslide warnings for four districts due to heavy rainfall.

title: Iran threatens ports in Mideast as US military set to impose shipping blockade
byline: The U.S. military announced it will begin a blockade of all Iranian ports and coastal areas on Monday, as President Donald Trump sought to pressure Iran in a move that risks driving oil prices even higher and renewing the war. The announcement set the stage for a showdown, as Iran immediately responded with threats on all ports in the Persian Gulf and the Gulf of Oman.

title: After criticizing Pope, Trump posts image of himself as a Jesus-like figure
byline: Shortly after criticizing Pope Leo XIV in a lengthy social media post on Sunday, President Trump shared an apparently A.I.-generated image depicting him as a Jesus-like figure.

title: Australia appoints woman to lead its army for the first time
byline: Australia on Monday said a woman would lead its army for the first time in history, as part of a reshuffle of ​the country’s defence force leadership.

title: Crowds gather ahead of iconic Indian singer’s funeral
byline: Crowds are gathering ahead of the funeral as tributes continue to pour in for Bollywood singing legend Asha Bhosle, who died at the age of 92.

title: Britney Spears goes into rehab after driving under the influence arrest
byline: Britney Spears has gone into rehab, a month after she was arrested on suspicion of driving under the influence of alcohol and drugs.

title: Oil jumps more than 7% to above $102 ahead of US blockade on Iran
byline: Oil prices jumped back above $100 a barrel on Monday as the U.S. Navy prepared ‌to block ships to and from Iran via the Strait of Hormuz, a move that could restrict Iranian oil exports, after Washington and Tehran failed to reach a deal to end the war.

title: ’Don’t fear him’: Pope Leo pushes back against Trump, says he won’t back down on war criticism
byline: Pope Leo on Monday pushed back against Trump, saying he did not fear him and would continue speaking out against war, including the conflict involving Iran, despite sharp criticism from the US president.

title: Large cocaine smuggling attempt stopped at BIA; Ugandan woman arrested
byline: Sri Lanka Customs officers have stopped a large cocaine smuggling attempt at the Bandaranaike International Airport (BIA) this morning, officials said.

title: Record prize money pot announced for Women’s T20 World Cup 2026
byline: The International Cricket Council (ICC) has announced a record prize fund of US$8,764,615 for the ICC Women’s T20 World Cup 2026, marking a 10% increase on the 2024 edition.

title: HRCSL finds FR violations in arrest, suspension of Thushara Upuldeniya
byline: The Human Rights Commission of Sri Lanka (HRCSL) has determined that the arrest and subsequent suspension of former Commissioner General of Prisons Thushara Upuldeniya amounted to violations of his Fundamental Rights, in connection with investigations into the alleged unlawful release of an inmate from the Anuradhapura Prison.

title: Peru’s presidential election delayed as voting chaos forces extension
byline: Peruvian voters will have to wait until at least Monday to learn the outcome of Sunday’s presidential election after the process was mired in logistical issues that left thousands of people in the country and abroad unable to cast ballots.

title: Fuel oil shipment arrives at Colombo port
byline: A shipment of fuel oil required for electricity generation arrived at the Colombo Port Dolphin Jetty last evening aboard the vessel Sea Adventure.

title: Audio clip on coal tender ‘Distorted’, says Lanka Coal Chairman
byline: The Lanka Coal Company (Pvt) Ltd has rejected claims circulating on social media regarding a telephone conversation linked to its emergency coal procurement process.

title: Gout Gout ’shakes’ athletics world after eclipsing Usain Bolt record
byline: Australian sprinter Gout Gout has stunned at the national athletics championships with a 200m time that eclipsed Usain Bolt’s under-20s record.

title: Festive food raids surge: 817 legal cases filed
byline: Public Health Inspectors (PHIs) have carried out 967 food safety raids islandwide during the ongoing festive season, resulting in 817 legal cases being filed against violators.

title: After 16 years in power, Hungarian Prime Minister concedes defeat
byline: Hungarian voters on Sunday ousted long-serving Prime Minister Viktor Orbán after 16 years in power, rejecting the authoritarian policies and global far-right movement that he embodied in favour of a pro-European challenger in a bombshell election result with global repercussions.

title: April 19 declared day of prayers for Easter Sunday attack victims
byline: The Catholic church in Sri Lanka has declared April 19, 2026 as a day of prayer for the victims of the Easter Sunday bomb attacks, Archbishop of Colombo Cardinal Malcolm Ranjith said today.

title: Orbán era swept away by Péter Magyar’s Hungary election landslide
byline: Viktor Orbán’s 16 years in power is over, and the system condemned as an ’’electoral autocracy’’ lies in tatters, defeated by a 45-year-old former party insider who convinced a majority of Hungarians to bring it to an end.

title: Engaging in work, transactions, and meals
byline: Following the sacred Nonagathaya period of the Sinhala New Year, normal activities resume at the auspicious time of 12:05 PM on April 14.

title: Pakistan proposes to host another round of talks in coming days before US-Iran truce ends
byline: Pakistan has proposed hosting a second round of talks between the United States and Iran in Islamabad in the coming days, before the end of the ceasefire, two Pakistani officials say.

title: Solar power users asked to turn off inverters until 3 PM today
byline: The National System Control Center has issued a special request to rooftop solar power system owners, asking them to voluntarily switch off their solar inverters today, April 14, until 3:00 PM.

title: US-sanctioned tankers pass Strait of Hormuz despite US blockade, data shows
byline: A Chinese tanker sanctioned by the United States ​passed through the Strait of Hormuz on ‌Tuesday despite a U.S. blockade on the chokepoint, shipping data showed.

title: Oil prices ease on hopes of new US-Iran peace talks
byline: Oil prices dipped in early Asian trade on Tuesday as hopes of more peace talks between the US and Iran eased concerns about further disruptions to energy supplies.

title: New Year food preparation begins
byline: As part of the Sinhala New Year celebrations, the preparation of food holds deep cultural and spiritual significance. On Tuesday, April 14, at 10:51 AM, families begin making traditional dishes such as milk rice (kiribath) and a variety of sweetmeats.

title: US vice president says ‘ball is in Iran’s court’ on deal to end war
byline: US Vice President JD Vance says the US would be happy to treat heavily-sanctioned Iran “like a normal country” if it doesn’t pursue nuclear weapons.

title: Russia’s oil revenue surges as sanctions relief eases during war on Iran
byline: JRussia’s revenue from oil exports almost doubled in March after Moscow received sanctions relief aimed at easing surging energy prices during the US-Israel war on Iran, according to the International Energy Agency.

title: North Korea tests cruise and anti-ship missiles from naval destroyer
byline: North Korea conducted another test of strategic cruise missiles and anti-warship missiles on Sunday as part of operational efficiency trials of its destroyer Choe Hyon, state media KCNA said on Tuesday.

title: Sunrisers Hyderabad pick Dilshan Madushanka as injury replacement
byline: Sunrisers Hyderabad (SRH) have picked Sri Lanka’s left-arm seamer Dilshan Madushanka as an injury replacement for Brydon Carse for the remainder of IPL 2026.

title: Iran demands compensation from 5 Arab states over alleged participation in US-Israeli strikes
byline: Iran demanded compensation from five Arab countries, including Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Bahrain, Qatar, and Jordan, accusing them of participating in US-Israeli strikes on Iran.

title: Italy suspends defence cooperation deal with Israel
byline: Italy’s Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said on Tuesday her government had ‌suspended a defence cooperation deal with Israel, reflecting frayed ties between previously close allies as the conflicts in the Middle East continue.

title: SLTB earns over Rs. 600 mn during New Year travel surge
byline: The Sri Lanka Transport Board (SLTB) has recorded a revenue of over Rs. 600 million from April 9 to 13, marking a significant increase in earnings during the Sinhala and Tamil New Year travel period.

title: US, Iran may resume talks this week despite port blockade
byline: Negotiating teams from the U.S. and Iran could return to Islamabad ​this week to resume talks to end the war, sources told Reuters on Tuesday, after the collapse of weekend negotiations prompted Washington to impose a blockade on Iranian ports.

title: China warns of countermeasures against US over tariff hikes threat
byline: China has threatened “countermeasures” if the US “goes ahead with the tariff hikes on China”, which Beijing says follow false media reports claiming it provided military support to Iran.

title: Gunman opens fire at high school in Turkey, wounding at least 16
byline: A former student opened fire at a high school in southeast Turkey on Tuesday, wounding at least 16 people before killing himself, an official said.

title: Japan halts new foreign worker intake for food services as quota nears
byline: Japan has stopped accepting new foreign workers in its food services sector from Monday (Apr 13), as the industry nears its quota under a skilled worker scheme.

title: Expressways generate Rs. 163 Mn revenue in three days
byline: Sri Lanka’s expressways recorded more than Rs. 163 million in revenue over a three-day period from April 10 to April 12, reflecting a surge in holiday travel, the Road Development Authority (RDA) said.

title: Former insider urges external leadership for SriLankan Airlines to root out entrenched corruption
byline: SriLankan Airlines is navigating a critical leadership transition as it prepares to appoint a new chairman and chief executive officer, a process that has sparked a fierce internal battle over the future direction of the national carrier.
